subject.title: [SECURITY] Privilege Escalation Vulnerability: docker Group Assignment Bypasses Hardening Measures

question: Should the hardened installer make rootless Docker the supported sandbox runtime, or adopt another mediated design that keeps the gateway account away from the rootful Docker socket?
rationale: The permanent fix changes the trust boundary and must preserve sandbox creation, one-command setup, reboot behavior, firewall guarantees, and upgrades; source inspection cannot safely choose that contract.

options.title: Adopt rootless Docker
options.body: Provision and validate a rootless daemon and socket for sandbox workloads, then migrate existing users out of the rootful docker group.

options.title: Build a sandbox broker
options.body: Keep rootful Docker behind a narrowly designed privileged service exposing only the operations and mounts required by OpenClaw sandboxes.

options.title: Accept and disclose authority
options.body: Retain Docker-group membership but explicitly document that compromise of the OpenClaw account compromises the host and narrow the hardening claims.

recommendation.title: Adopt rootless Docker
recommendation.body: Provision and validate a rootless daemon and socket for sandbox workloads, then migrate existing users out of the rootful docker group.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across installer lifecycle, user handling, service setup, and merged changes in the affected area.
